# Introduction

<!--In this section you explain what you are trying to show.  Where did the data come from?  What is the research or other question you are trying to answer?.  If you skimp in this section expect to be marked down in your grade. Paint a picture of the project a couple of paragraphs is expected!-->

A new  preventative aides drug (triUmpsal) is under test in clinical trials. Consider only the females, does this drug seem effective?  Hint - use dplyr to obtain that subpopulation with the filter command.

The question is whether the drug triUmpsal appears to make a difference when compared with a placebo.Focusing mainly on female participants in the clinical trial. By comparing the infection outcomes of females who received triUmpsal with those who received a placebo.to find out if the relationships between the treatment received and the likelihood of becoming infected. And to determine if the data provides evidence that triUmpsal may be an effective preventative treatment for females.

$H_0$ there is No, relationship between treatment either triumpsal or placebo and infection satus among female participants.  
$H_A$ There is a relationship between treatment either triUmpsal or placebo and infection status among females participants.  


```{r}
femaleData <- triUmp %>%
  filter(gender == "F")

names(femaleData)

table(femaleData$treatment)
```

# Methods  

we use two categorical variables. Treatment identifies whether female participants received triUmpsal or a placebo. infection status identifies whether participants became infected with AIDS or remained uninfected.  

Categorical-treatment  

categorical- infection status.

# Results

## Descriptive Results

### Graphical Descriptive Results

```{r}
barchartGC(~treatment+ infected, data=femaleData)
barchartGC(~treatment + infected, data=femaleData, type="percent")

```

The first bar graph illustrates the frequency of infected and uninfected female participants from the drug and placebo groups. The graph demonstrates that 210 females who received triUmpsal became infected, compared to 147 females who received the placebo.However, because the two treatment groups contain different number of participants the % graph provides stronger data.The second graph shows that 3.69% of females in the drug group became infected, compared to 2.42% in the placebo group. showing that the % of infected participants was higher among those who received triUmpsal.
